stanzas.sanskrit:
ततश्च बृन्दावनतोऽतिदूरतो
वनं गतस्त्वं खलु गोपगोकुलैः ।
हृदन्तरे भक्ततरद्विजाङ्गना-
-कदम्बकानुग्रहणाग्रहं वहन् ॥ ६१-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One day, Krishna along with his brother Balarama, Gopas and cows went little far away in to the forest from Vrindavan. He had planned to give blessings to the Brahmin women who were all devoted to Him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tataśca bṛndāvanato’tidūrato
vanaṃ gatastvaṃ khalu gopagokulaiḥ |
hṛdantare bhaktataradvijāṅganā-
-kadambakānugrahaṇāgrahaṃ vahan || 61-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततो निरीक्ष्याशरणे वनान्तरे
किशोरलोकं क्षुधितं तृषाकुलम् ।
अदूरतो यज्ञपरान् द्विजान् प्रति
व्यसर्जयो दीदिवियाचनाय तान् ॥ ६१-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: As they wandered deep in to the forest, Gopas felt tired and hungry and wanted food to eat and water to quench their thirst. Krishna directed them to go to the Brahmins who were doing yagnya nearby and ask for food.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tato nirīkṣyāśaraṇe vanāntare
kiśoralokaṃ kṣudhitaṃ tṛṣākulam |
adūrato yajñaparān dvijān prati
vyasarjayo dīdiviyācanāya tān || 61-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
गतेष्वथो तेष्वभिधाय तेऽभिधां
कुमारकेष्वोदनयाचिषु प्रभो ।
श्रुतिस्थिरा अप्यभिनिन्युरश्रुतिं
न किञ्चिदूचुश्च महीसुरोत्तमाः ॥ ६१-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The boys then went to the Brahmins and they mentioned Krishna’s name and asked for food. But the great Brahmins who were known to be well versed in Vedas acted as if they had not heard anything and did not respond in any manner.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gateṣvatho teṣvabhidhāya te’bhidhāṃ
kumārakeṣvodanayāciṣu prabho |
śrutisthirā apyabhininyuraśrutiṃ
na kiñcidūcuśca mahīsurottamāḥ || 61-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अनादरात् खिन्नधियो हि बालकाः
समाययुर्युक्तमिदं हि यज्वसु ।
चिरादभक्ताः खलु ते महीसुराः
कथं हि भक्तं त्वयि तैः समर्प्यते ॥ ६१-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas were saddened at heart at being ignored by the Brahmins and returned disappointed. This act of the ritualistic Brahmins who were not devoted to Lord for a long time, was expected. When they are not devoted, how they will offer food to Bhagwan?
stanzas.stanza_roman:
anādarāt khinnadhiyo hi bālakāḥ
samāyayuryuktamidaṃ hi yajvasu |
cirādabhaktāḥ khalu te mahīsurāḥ
kathaṃ hi bhaktaṃ tvayi taiḥ samarpyate || 61-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
निवेदयध्वं गृहिणीजनाय मां
दिशेयुरन्नं करुणाकुला इमाः ।
इति स्मितार्द्रं भवतेरिता गता-
-स्ते दारका दारजनं ययाचिरे ॥ ६१-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna then told the gopas to go to the wives of those brahmins and ask for food. Krishna smilingly told them that the vipra pathnis were full of compassion and that they would give food. Hence the gopas went to the vipra pathnis and asked for food.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nivedayadhvaṃ gṛhiṇījanāya māṃ
diśeyurannaṃ karuṇākulā imāḥ |
iti smitārdraṃ bhavateritā gatā-
-ste dārakā dārajanaṃ yayācire || 61-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
गृहीतनाम्नि त्वयि सम्भ्रमाकुला-
-श्चतुर्विधं भोज्यरसं प्रगृह्य ताः ।
चिरं धृतत्वत्प्रविलोकनाग्रहाः
स्वकैर्निरुद्धा अपि तूर्णमाययुः ॥ ६१-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: When Gopas took Krishna's name, the wives of the Brahnmins became excited. They had desired to see Krishna for a long time. Inspite of being forbidden by their husbands, the women carried four types of food offering and came to see Krishna quickly.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gṛhītanāmni tvayi sambhramākulā-
-ścaturvidhaṃ bhojyarasaṃ pragṛhya tāḥ |
ciraṃ dhṛtatvatpravilokanāgrahāḥ
svakairniruddhā api tūrṇamāyayuḥ || 61-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
विलोलपिञ्छं चिकुरे कपोलयोः
समुल्लसत्कुण्डलमार्द्रमीक्षिते ।
निधाय बाहुं सुहृदंससीमनि
स्थितं भवन्तं समलोकयन्त ताः ॥ ६१-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The vipra pathnis were delighted to see Krishna with cheeks glowing with the reflection of the dancing ear-drops, beautiful peacock feathers in his crown and standing with His arms around his friend's shoulder.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vilolapiñchaṃ cikure kapolayoḥ
samullasatkuṇḍalamārdramīkṣite |
nidhāya bāhuṃ suhṛdaṃsasīmani
sthitaṃ bhavantaṃ samalokayanta tāḥ || 61-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तदा च काचित् त्वदुपागमोद्यता
गृहीतहस्ता दयितेन यज्वना ।
तदैव सञ्चिन्त्य भवन्तमञ्जसा
विवेश कैवल्यमहो कृतिन्यसौ ॥ ६१-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One of the vipra pathni was being prevented by her ritualistic husband to go near Krishna to meeting Him. She meditated deeply on Krishna at that place itself and merged with Krishna, attaining salvation. How fortunate, She is?!
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadā ca kācit tvadupāgamodyatā
gṛhītahastā dayitena yajvanā |
tadaiva sañcintya bhavantamañjasā
viveśa kaivalyamaho kṛtinyasau || 61-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आदाय भोज्यान्यनुगृह्य ताः पुन-
-स्त्वदङ्गसङ्गस्पृहयोज्झतीर्गृहम् ।
विलोक्य यज्ञाय विसर्जयन्निमा-
-श्चकर्थ भर्तॄनपि तास्वगर्हणान् ॥ ६१-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna took their offerings and blessed them. The vipra pathnis desired to be with Krishna and so abandoned their houses. Krishna sent them back to conduct the Yagya rituals properly. He asked the husbands, not to have ill feelings towards their wives.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ādāya bhojyānyanugṛhya tāḥ puna-
-stvadaṅgasaṅgaspṛhayojjhatīrgṛham |
vilokya yajñāya visarjayannimā-
-ścakartha bhartṝnapi tāsvagarhaṇān || 61-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
निरूप्य दोषं निजमङ्गनाजने
विलोक्य भक्तिं च पुनर्विचारिभिः ।
प्रबुद्धतत्त्वैस्त्वमभिष्टुतो द्विजै-
-र्मरुत्पुराधीश निरुन्धि मे गदान् ॥ ६१-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
The Brahmins realised their own mistake. They also recognized the great devotion of their wives to Bhagwan. They reflected upon themselves, realised the paramatma and sang in his praise.
Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan, who blessed the vipra pathnis, to eradicate all his sufferings.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nirūpya doṣaṃ nijamaṅganājane
vilokya bhaktiṃ ca punarvicāribhiḥ |
prabuddhatattvaistvamabhiṣṭuto dvijai-
-rmarutpurādhīśa nirundhi me gadān || 61-10 ||
